extraction.method: Complete PDF text extraction by page to adjacent .txt files; page labels retained. SHA-256 is of the downloaded PDF bytes. A complete extraction does not imply that every page of a book/chapter was read; read_ranges records actual reading.

sources.title: 18.650 Statistics for Applications, Lecture 10: Generalized Linear Models (GLMs)
sources.edition_or_date: Fall 2016; original course PDF metadata dated November 2016
sources.access: Official public university course notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-53, complete focused lecture text.
anchors: PDF pp. 10-21: exponential-family representation, derivatives of the log normalizer, and mean/variance identities.
PDF pp. 23-33: links, canonical link, likelihood, score/Hessian structure, and concavity; retain existence and rank qualifications.
PDF pp. 40-52: logistic likelihood, score/Hessian, Fisher scoring and the IRLS construction.
PDF p. 37 contains an overbroad generic Newton convergence statement; do not reuse it. The lecture contains no GLM deviance-residual derivation.
sources.proof_limits: This is a lecture unit, not a general existence or convergence theorem. Complete separation can prevent a finite logistic MLE. Do not treat the last weighted least-squares step of IRLS as an inferential theorem.

sources.title: Statistics for Applications, Lecture 4: Multivariate Normal Distribution and CLT
sources.access: Official public university course notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-4, complete focused lecture text.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-3: vector expectation/covariance, affine covariance transform, Gaussian density for nonsingular covariance, singular-support caveat, and affine images.
PDF p. 4: orthogonal invariance of iid standard-normal coordinates, proved by the joint-density change-of-variables argument.
PDF p. 4: multivariate CLT is stated without proof and is not used for any exact finite-sample law.
sources.proof_limits: The density derivation requires positive-definite covariance; singular cases are described on their support. The orthogonal-coordinate proof is direct and serves as an independent route for the linear-model decomposition.

sources.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
sources.edition_or_date: Fall 2006; direct course PDF is 11 pages and internally headed Section 15
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-11, complete focused lecture text.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-2: fixed-design Gaussian model, full-column-rank hypothesis n>p, least-squares/MLE normal equations, and variance MLE RSS/n.
PDF pp. 2-5: distribution of beta_hat and residual sum of squares; economy QR, orthogonal completion, independence, and chi-square with n-p degrees of freedom.
PDF pp. 5-7: normal contrasts, exact t and F pivots, joint confidence ellipsoid, and subset-parameter tests.
PDF pp. 8-11: regression examples and collinearity interpretation.
sources.proof_limits: The full-rank hypothesis is essential for coefficient uniqueness and inverse formulas. Re-express the source's variance MLE RSS/n separately from the unbiased residual variance RSS/(n-p). A few OCR-rendered symbols are damaged; formulas were checked against the PDF text and independent sources.

sources.title: Statistics: Lecture Three — Linear Models
sources.institution: University of California, Berkeley, Department of Statistics (course material linked from Statistics 230A)
sources.edition_or_date: Public lecture notes; PDF metadata creation date August 2006; 19 pages
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university course notes; no extra license claim made here.
anchors: PDF pp. 2-5: model matrix, least-squares geometry, normal equations, fitted/residual projections, estimability, and coefficient covariance.
PDF p. 6: Gauss-Markov proof by decomposing a competing linear unbiased estimator into the OLS component and an orthogonal remainder.
PDF pp. 6-7: normal-theory distributions and coefficient/F inference stated; use MIT's full decomposition proof for exact independence and pivot laws.
PDF p. 8: practice workflow and residual-versus-fitted, predictor, omitted-variable, and time plots; pp. 11-12 and 17: diagnostic/extension examples; p. 19: concise GLS and GLM introduction.
sources.proof_limits: Some variance algebra on p. 5 is not cleanly written; the p. 6 Gauss-Markov proof is the preferred route. The note treats diagnostics as checks, not proof of model assumptions.

sources.title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis in the Real and Complex Domains, Chapter 3: The Multivariate Gaussian and Related Distributions
sources.access: Official open-access chapter; the book is OA. Chapter 9 explicitly states CC BY 4.0; this record does not extend that chapter-specific statement beyond verified chapter terms.
anchors: Whole chapter: real multivariate Gaussian definition/density, linear transformations, marginal and conditional distributions, independence, and quadratic forms.
PDF pp. 55-56 (book pp. 183-184): orthogonal transformation route to independence of sample mean and centered scatter for a Gaussian sample.
PDF pp. 61-62 (book pp. 189-190): maximum-likelihood estimates for multivariate normal mean and covariance and denominator distinction.
sources.proof_limits: The chapter includes extensive complex-domain material that is not used. Some displayed matrix transposes and conditional-density transcription are suspect; use only independently checked real formulas. Generic asymptotic likelihood discussion is not a substitute for the Cat1 regular Wilks theorem.

sources.title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis in the Real and Complex Domains, Chapter 5: Matrix-Variate Gamma and Beta Distributions, Section 5.5: The Wishart Density
sources.access: Official open-access chapter in the Springer OA book; no claim that every chapter-specific reuse term was checked.
sources.read_ranges: Only Section 5.5, PDF pp. 47-66 (book pp. 335-354), was read; the other 85 extracted pages were not read for this assignment.
anchors: PDF pp. 47-51: Wishart density setup and gamma-integral normalization.
PDF pp. 52-57: triangularization, sample covariance as a Wishart matrix, and the change-of-variables proof route.
PDF pp. 57-66: additivity, congruence/linear image, determinant, marginal and Schur-complement properties.
sources.proof_limits: The chapter is matrix-calculus dense; the dossier relies on the real normal-sample Wishart route and states the degrees of freedom directly. The chapter is not claimed as fully read.

sources.title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis in the Real and Complex Domains, Chapter 6: Hypothesis Testing and Null Distributions
sources.access: Official open-access chapter in the Springer OA book; no claim that every chapter-specific reuse term was checked.
sources.read_ranges: Focused complete sections: PDF pp. 20-36 (Section 6.3, book pp. 414-430) and PDF pp. 37-42 (Section 6.4, book pp. 431-436). Partial reading only: PDF pp. 43-46 (start of Section 6.5, book pp. 437-440) and pp. 69-72 (selected pages of Section 6.10, book pp. 463-466). Other pages were not read for this assignment.
anchors: Section 6.3, PDF pp. 20-36: likelihood-ratio test of a Gaussian mean vector with unknown covariance; exact Hotelling T-squared to F transformation and one-/two-sample extensions.
Section 6.4, PDF pp. 37-42: covariance-matrix null test, trace chi-square alternative under the null, likelihood ratio, and regular asymptotic chi-square dimension p(p+1)/2.
Section 6.5 start, PDF pp. 43-46, and selected Section 6.10 pp. 69-72 are partial context only; no complete claim is based on them.
sources.proof_limits: The Hotelling result depends on the Wishart/sample-mean laws and a matrix gamma integral; use the checked real-case derivation and independent statement cautiously. The trace chi-square statistic is not the covariance likelihood-ratio statistic. Asymptotic likelihood calibration is Cat1 material, and covariance boundary/null hypotheses require explicit regularity.

sources.title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis in the Real and Complex Domains, Chapter 9: Principal Component Analysis
sources.access: Official open-access chapter licensed CC BY 4.0, as stated by Springer.
anchors: PDF pp. 2-5 (book pp. 598-601): Rayleigh-quotient optimization and eigenvector proof for the leading principal component, then orthogonal successive components.
PDF pp. 8-15: covariance-versus-correlation scaling, explained variance, and deterministic component properties.
PDF pp. 15-25: sample PCA and sample-matrix formulation.
PDF pp. 24-42: Gaussian/Wishart eigenvalue distributions; derivations rely on matrix Jacobian material not completed within this focused treatment.
sources.proof_limits: The sign of an eigenvector is never identified, and a repeated eigenvalue identifies a subspace rather than a unique component. One printed third-eigenvalue variance expression is a typo. The dossier uses only the deterministic optimization and scaling results, not the lengthy eigenvalue laws.

sources.title: Generalized Linear Models, Advanced Methods for Data Analysis (36-402/36-608)
sources.institution: Carnegie Mellon University, Department of Statistics
sources.access: Instructor-posted public course note; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-6, complete focused lecture text.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-4: GLM components, exponential-family form, Bernoulli/Poisson/Gaussian examples, canonical links, and likelihood.
PDF p. 5: independent-observation log likelihood and IRLS as an algorithmic Fisher-scoring form.
PDF p. 6: additive-model extension, read but not used.
sources.proof_limits: This note is an independent check of family/link/likelihood formulas, not a full proof of score or IRLS inference. Its advice to infer from the final weighted least-squares step is not used.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 1 Notes: The Problem of Correlated Data
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.edition_or_date: STA 610, Fall 2026; lecture note dated August 2026 in PDF metadata
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-11, complete focused lecture note.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-3: OLS exogeneity, full rank, covariance under general error covariance, and BLUE assumptions.
PDF pp. 4-8: random-intercept covariance derivation, compound symmetry, and why OLS is no longer BLUE when errors are correlated.
PDF pp. 8-11: intraclass correlation, design effect, and inferential consequences.
sources.proof_limits: These notes support covariance and design consequences; they do not prove the general linear mixed-model likelihood theory.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 3: One-Way ANOVA and the Hierarchical Normal Model
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-9, complete focused lecture note.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-4: balanced one-way fixed- and random-effects ANOVA, expected mean squares, and sums-of-squares decomposition.
PDF pp. 4-7: moment estimators for variance components with derivation and balanced/unbalanced formulas.
PDF pp. 8-9: boundary/negative unconstrained component estimate caveat and examples.
sources.proof_limits: The note contains a later Bayesian shrinkage reference; it is not used. Negative unconstrained moment estimates are not valid variance parameters and must be reported as a limitation, not silently clipped.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 4: MLE and Inference for the Hierarchical Normal Model
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.access: Official course page links to instructor-posted notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-6, complete focused lecture note; the PDF is the Lecture 4 MLE/REML note linked from the course page.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-3: marginal Gaussian likelihood for a hierarchical normal model and profile likelihood for variance components.
PDF pp. 3-5: exact balanced one-way MLE biases, REML as likelihood of error contrasts, and equality with ANOVA estimates in the balanced case.
PDF p. 6: variance-component inference caveats.
sources.proof_limits: Use REML's error-contrast definition and balanced identity only; do not import optimization implementation or broad variance-component testing approximations.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 5: Estimation of Group Effects
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-11 read. Non-Bayesian frequentist BLUP focus: pp. 8-10 (Sections 4.1-4.5). Bayesian-posterior material on pp. 10-11 was read to identify and exclude it.
anchors: PDF pp. 8-10, Sections 4.1-4.5: BLUP and empirical BLUP formulas under stated moment assumptions.
PDF pp. 10-11: explicitly Bayesian perspective, read but excluded from the category-2 model dependencies.
sources.proof_limits: The note gives the BLUP result without a full best-linear-unbiased proof. Derive it in the model page by the existing affine L2 projection/covariance normal equations or the Gaussian conditional-mean identity. Empirical BLUP inherits variance-parameter estimation uncertainty and is not the known-parameter BLUP theorem.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 6: Linear Mixed-Effects Models
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-16, complete focused lecture note; computational fitting discussion read but excluded as a dependency.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-4: general LME model Y_j=X_j beta+Z_j b_j+e_j, random intercept/slope structures and their covariance.
PDF pp. 4-9: marginal covariance, GLS fixed-effect estimation, and matrix BLUP formulas.
PDF pp. 10-16: identifiability, covariance-model choices, boundary and estimation caveats.
sources.proof_limits: Use the Gaussian model and covariance/GLS equations only. Numerical fitting, implementation, and Bayesian language are excluded; variance components on the boundary invalidate ordinary interior likelihood approximations.

sources.title: STA610 Lecture 7: The Longitudinal Linear Mixed Model
authors: Fan Li (course instructor; note credited to STA610)
sources.institution: Duke University, Department of Statistical Science
sources.access: Instructor-posted public university notes; no extra license claim made here.
sources.read_ranges: PDF pp. 1-21, complete focused lecture note. The missing-data discussion was read but is explicitly excluded from models-01 scope.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-7: longitudinal mean models, random intercept/slope time terms, marginal covariance, and conditional/marginal interpretation.
PDF pp. 8-13: residual covariance structures including independence, compound symmetry, AR(1), Toeplitz and unstructured forms.
PDF pp. 14-21: time/baseline modeling, visit patterns and missingness context; missing-data theorems are excluded from this category.
sources.proof_limits: The 'MAR-valid LMM' language is not a theorem for arbitrary missingness or model misspecification; do not import missing-data dependencies from this note into category 2.

sources.title: Multivariate Analysis, 2021, Lecture 2: Review of Multivariate Distribution Theory
sources.access: Lecturer-hosted public notes; license not stated on the note.
anchors: PDF p. 1: conditional multivariate normal mean/covariance and independence criterion, but proof methods are outlines only.
PDF pp. 2-3: Wishart definition and listed properties; several are set as exercises/checks rather than proved.
sources.proof_limits: Secondary formula check only; do not rely on the proof gaps as a primary theorem source.

sources.title: Multivariate Analysis, 2021, Lecture 3: Cochran's and Craig's Theorem and Some Distributions
sources.access: Lecturer-hosted public notes; license not stated on the note.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-3: sufficient half of Cochran's theorem, normal sample scatter/Wishart, and independence statements.
PDF pp. 3-5: Hotelling T-squared and exact F conversion; proof references an inverse-Wishart quadratic-form result not proved in the note.
sources.proof_limits: The necessary half of Cochran is explicitly omitted; the proof of transformed-coordinate independence is left as an exercise. The source is a cross-check, not the load-bearing exact-inference proof.

sources.title: Multivariate Analysis, 2021, Lecture 7: On Some Multivariate Testing Methods
sources.access: Lecturer-hosted public notes; license not stated on the note.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-2: multivariate Gaussian MLE formulas and likelihood-ratio testing setup.
PDF pp. 2-4: Wilks theorem statement and testing examples.
sources.proof_limits: Wilks theorem is stated with its proof deferred; use Cat1 MSF-15 for regular asymptotic calibration. The note is a secondary formula check only.

sources.title: Multivariate Analysis, 2021, Lecture 8: Principal Component Analysis
sources.access: Lecturer-hosted public notes; license not stated on the note.
anchors: PDF pp. 1-2: likelihood-ratio and invariant-test context for covariance hypotheses.
PDF pp. 2-4: PCA eigenvalue/eigenvector formulation and top-direction argument.
sources.proof_limits: The second-component optimization is left as an exercise; covariance-test formulas and Gaussian eigenvalue laws are summarized rather than fully derived. Use Springer Chapter 9 and existing spectral items for deterministic PCA.

coverage_note: All 19 PDF source files listed above were completely extracted with fitz. Focused reading completeness varies by unit exactly as recorded; two Springer chapters were read only in their named sections, not as whole chapters. The source dossier records all theorem/proof limits and excluded Bayesian/computational material.
